calls.head: Bedard gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lindholm’s line (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Blackhawks’ first line is Kantserov, Bedard and Teräväinen.

surprises.head: Chicago flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Chicago gets outshot more than almost anyone. Not tonight: Chicago took 55 of the 93 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Chicago would expect about 43%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Lohrei sparks a Bruins comeback
paras: Anton Frondell struck first for the Blackhawks on the power play early in the first, with Patrick Kane picking up his 900th NHL assist on the goal. David Pastrňák made it 1-1 for Boston midway through the period. Frondell scored his second of the night early in the second to put the Hawks back ahead 2-1. Casey Mittelstadt tied it up for Boston midway through the period. It was a busy third period. Ryan Greene and Connor Bedard scored less than three minutes apart midway through the period to put the Blackhawks up 4-2. Mason Lohrei cut Chicago’s lead to 4-3, 46 seconds later. With the goalie pulled and 12 seconds left, Morgan Geekie tied it 4-4. Elias Lindholm won it two and a half minutes into overtime.
Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Michael DiPietro made 37 saves for the Bruins, and Arvid Söderblom allowed five goals on 32 shots.

Alex Vlasic took three penalties on his own. The officials called 14 penalties, a total the league sees about once every 40 games. The Bruins improved to 10-4-1, still first in the Atlantic, while the Blackhawks fell to 4-9-1, still last in the Central.

items.text: David Pastrňák passed Patrice Bergeron for third on the Bruins’ all-time goals list, with 428.
Connor Bedard has a point in five straight games.
The Blackhawks have gone winless in six straight on the road.
The Bruins bounced back after two straight losses.
